label: Bible Study
prompt: And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in _____ seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.
verse: And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.
note: Naaman wanted a showy healing — he got told to take seven dips in the Jordan, and stormed off insulted.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into _____, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
verse: And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
note: Swords into plowshares, spears into pruninghooks — Micah's picture of a world that's finished with war.

label: Sunday School
prompt: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my _____.
verse: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.
note: The origin of 'by the skin of my teeth' — Job, describing how barely he'd escaped.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the _____ of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
verse: For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
note: Israel traded a spring of living water for leaky handmade tanks — the two evils in one picture.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: My son, despise not the _____ of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:
verse: My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:
note: Don't despise the LORD's 'chastening' — Hebrews 12:5–6 quotes this to show that discipline is proof of sonship.
